title: Harness support
description: Formal shape of an adapter's support declaration, `.pkit/adapters/<name>/harness-support.yaml` (COR-047 point 2): how far the adapter's harness meets each harness requirement the core declares in harness-requirements.yaml. `pkit harness report` resolves the answers for a project; `pkit validate` checks each declaration against this shape. harness-support.yaml beside this file is the documented empty shape. Companion per COR-018 / the .pkit/schemas/ area conventions.

requirements.description: One answer per core harness requirement the adapter answers, keyed by the requirement's id in harness-requirements.yaml. A requirement left out resolves indeterminate, never satisfied (COR-047 point 3).

answer.description: The adapter's answer to one harness requirement (COR-047 point 2).

grade.description: How far the harness meets the requirement, in the vocabulary the adapters README owns: supported — the harness provides the behaviour, nothing more asked of the adopter; at-cost — achievable, at the cost `cost` names; not-achievable — not achievable on this harness at all, whatever its configuration.

cost.description: For an at-cost answer, and only for one: what the adopter pays for the behaviour to hold — a configuration, a discipline, a platform.

harness_versions.description: The harness versions the answer holds for. `unbounded`: every version, as the author asserts. [lowest, highest], both included: the versions the author tested it on. []: no version yet, so the answer covers none. Required, so no answer widens to every version by an edit that drops it: only an author who has tested the claim widens it, never a tool (COR-047 point 2).

evidence.description: How the adapter's author knows the answer: a measurement, a test, the harness's documentation.
